I couldn't find any argument and log="y" doesn't work.

Thanks.

messages.subject: Release of seewave 2.0.4
messages.body_plain:
Dear seewave users,

A new version of seewave (2.0.4) has been pushed to CRAN right now. The
version of each OS should be available soon.

Please see the changes listed below.

Thanks to Andrey Anikin, Daniel Ridley-Ellis, Pavel Senin for their help!

Enjoy your summer recordings,

Jerome

NEW FUNCTIONS
	o bwfilter(): a new function to apply a Butterworth filter, based on
butter() and filtfilt() of the package signal.
	o melfilterbank(): a new function to compute and display mel-filters
used to compute MFCCs.
	o phaseplot2(): a new function to display a time wave against a delayed
version of itself (phase-phase space).
	o preemphasis(): a new function to apply a speech pre-emphasis filter.

NEW ARGUMENTS
	o ceps(): a new argument 'phase' to take into account the phase of the
signal.
	o meanspec(), spec(), spectro(), spectro3D(): a new argument
'correction' to apply a correction factor (either amplitude or energy
correction) on the taper window so that either amplitude or energy is
preserved from the time signal to the frequency spectrum.
	o spec(): a new argument 'scaled' to scale the results to the length of
the FFT ; a small bug regarding frequency scale fixed when 'at' is NULL.

OTHER CHANGES
         o attenuation(): a bug introduced in the previous version is
now fixed.
	o cepstro(): the value $amp is transposed such that columns correspond
correctly to successive cepstra.
	o cutspec(): is now more accurate.
	o dfreq(): a small bug regarding frequency scale fixed.
	o dynspec(): a bug with the zero padding (argument 'zp') fixed. Thanks
to Andrey Anikin.
	o echo(): is now faster.
	o env(..., envt="hil",...): is now faster.
	o fir(): is now faster.
	o fma(): is now faster.
	o hilbert(): is now faster.
	o ifreq(): is now faster.
	o Q(): a bug fixed when the input was a frequency spectrum cut with
cutspec(). The interpolation is changed to increase to resolution.
Thanks to Daniel Ridley-Ellis.
	o rmam(): is now faster.
	o SAX(): an improvement for unevenly broken segments. Thanks to Pavel
Senin.
	o songmeter(): now handles SM4 model.
	o spectro(): a bug with the zero padding (argument 'zp') fixed, Thanks
to Andrey Anikin. A new logical argument 'flog' to plot the frequency
axis on a log scale.
	o spectro3D(): a bug with the zero padding (argument 'zp') fixed.
Thanks to Andrey Anikin.
	o symba(): the value of the sequence of symbols of the 'y' is now
correctly named 's2' instead of 's1'; the computation of the entropy of
y has been corrected implying a correction in the computation of the
mutual information I; the plot of y has been corrected; 'absolute
frequency' has been corrected to 'relative frequency' in the documentation.
	o TKEO(): a mistake in the documentation regarding the exponent and lag
parameters is now fixed.
	o wf(): it is now possible to combine different waterfall displays in a
multiframe graphic (using for instance layout()). A bug with the zero
padding (argument 'zp') fixed. Thanks to Andrey Anikin.
	o zcr(): a mistake in the documentation regarding the definition of the
sign function is now fixed.

messages.subject: meanspec() units and usage
messages.body_plain:
Hello!

Hello!
I am working on a project where I would like to compare the spectral distribution of energy before and after the playback of a predator cue.

>From the long recording, I extract am extracting one chunk of sound before the event occurs ("Before_event") and a second chunk of sound from after the event occurs ("After_event"). To extract the spectral information from these recordings, I am using the following code

before_spec<-meanspec(Before_event, f=300000, ovlp=90, plot=FALSE, dB=NULL, norm=FALSE)
after_spec <-meanspec(After_event, f=300000, ovlp=90, plot=FALSE, dB=NULL, norm=FALSE)

And then I will test for differences between these extracted spectra.

Two questions:
1. I have not been able to find the units for the data frame returned by mean spec. Is the unit mV?
2. I would like the returned value to represent absolute energy in each frequency bin over the duration of the recording. I have tried to write the code in a way that achieves this without normalization, but if this is not correct, I would be very grateful to know.

Thank you very much for your time, thoughts, and suggestions,
Laurel

messages.subject: Re: [seewave] meanspec() units and usage
messages.body_plain:
Dear Laurel,

1. I have not been able to find the units for the data frame returned by mean spec. Is the unit mV?

No, there are no units. If you add correction="amplitude" (I alsor remove dB=NULL which is a default seeting), you should have values that correspond to the amplitude values of your original sound, along a 2^16 scale if your file was digitized with a 16 bit depth.

before_spec<-meanspec(Before_event, f=300000, ovlp=90, plot=FALSE, correction="amplitude", norm=FALSE)
after_spec <-meanspec(After_event, f=300000, ovlp=90, plot=FALSE, correction="amplitude", norm=FALSE)

2. I would like the returned value to represent absolute energy in each frequency bin over the duration of the recording. I have tried to write the code in a way that achieves this without normalization, but if this is not correct, I would be very grateful to know.

I think that the code above should do the job. But be aware that meanspec() computes an average of your data so that you transform in a certain way your data.

HTH

Jerome

messages.subject: Calculating entropy index (H)
messages.body_plain:
Hi everybody,

I'm trying to determine the entropy index for a sample, and I'm not sure if I'm correctly calculating the PMF for the amplitude envelope. Here's my code:

n = 1.44e6

#amplitude envelope

t_env = env(tr1_upa, f = 48000, envt = "hil", plot = FALSE, norm = FALSE)

#pmf of amplitude envelope

t_env_pmf = abs(t_env)/sum(abs(t_env))

#temporal entropy (Ht)
Ht = -sum(t_env_pmf * log2(t_env_pmf)*(log2(n))^-1)

#frequency spectrum

m_s = meanspec(tr1_upa, f = 48000, wl = 512, PMF = TRUE, ovlp = 25)

#spectral entropy (Hf)
Hf = -sum(m_s[,2] * log2(m_s[,2]) * log2(512)^-1)

#acoustic diversity (H)
H = Hf * Ht

Am I on the right track?

Thanks,

Sean Hardison

messages.subject: " Warning message: In n_recs * f : NAs produced by integer overflow" 90Mb Limit for soundscapespec?
messages.subject_clean: " Warning message: In n_recs * f : NAs produced by integer overflow" 90Mb Limit for soundscapespec?
messages.body_plain:
Where Wav file is > ~90 Mb (48k, 16bit, stereo files)

> test<-readWave("test~91Mb.wav")

>soundscapespec(test,  plot=TRUE, col="darkgreen")

> Warning message:
> In n_recs * f : NAs produced by integer overflow

Smaller wav files do not exhibit this behaviour; further testing reveals the cut-off to be about 90 Mb.

Which is an unfortunate length for some musical audio.

Any chance of a slight expansion on the type to something a bit bigger?

Many thanks :)

messages.subject: Re: [seewave] " Warning message: In n_recs * f : NAs produced by integer overflow" 90Mb Limit for soundscapespec?
messages.subject_clean: [seewave] " Warning message: In n_recs * f : NAs produced by integer overflow" 90Mb Limit for soundscapespec?
messages.body_plain:
Dear Seggie,

One step of the process of computing this frequency spectrum consists
in scaling the STFT by the number of FFTs * sampling frequency.

With a long sound this number might overpass the integer limits of R.

A solution could be (not tried) to reduce the number of FFTs by
increasing the FFT length (wl) and/or decreasing the overlap between
successive FFTs (ovlp).

HTH

Jerome

On Tue, Jul 26, 2016 at 10:41 AM, Jérôme SUEUR <su...@mnhn.fr> wrote:

> Dear Seggie,
>
> One step of the process of computing this frequency spectrum consists in scaling the STFT by the number of FFTs * sampling frequency.
>
> With a long sound this number might overpass the integer limits of R.
>
> A solution could be (not tried) to reduce the number of FFTs by increasing the FFT length (wl) and/or decreasing the overlap between successive FFTs (ovlp).
>
> HTH
>
> Jerome
>

messages.subject: Re: [seewave] meanspec() units and usage
messages.body_plain:
That is quite useful. Thank you very much!

On Friday, July 22, 2016 at 8:11:10 AM UTC-4, ECO ACOUSTICS wrote:
> Dear Laurel,
>
> 1. I have not been able to find the units for the data frame returned by mean spec. Is the unit mV?
>
> No, there are no units. If you add correction="amplitude" (I alsor remove dB=NULL which is a default seeting), you should have values that correspond to the amplitude values of your original sound, along a 2^16 scale if your file was digitized with a 16 bit depth.
>
> before_spec<-meanspec(Before_event, f=300000, ovlp=90, plot=FALSE, correction="amplitude", norm=FALSE)
> after_spec <-meanspec(After_event, f=300000, ovlp=90, plot=FALSE, correction="amplitude", norm=FALSE)
>
> 2. I would like the returned value to represent absolute energy in each frequency bin over the duration of the recording. I have tried to write the code in a way that achieves this without normalization, but if this is not correct, I would be very grateful to know.
>
> I think that the code above should do the job. But be aware that meanspec() computes an average of your data so that you transform in a certain way your data.
>
> HTH
>
> Jerome
>
>
>
> Le 18/07/2016 à 22:35, Laurel Symes a écrit :
> > Hello!
> >
> > Hello!
> > I am working on a project where I would like to compare the spectral distribution of energy before and after the playback of a predator cue.
> >
> > From the long recording, I extract am extracting one chunk of sound before the event occurs ("Before_event") and a second chunk of sound from after the event occurs ("After_event"). To extract the spectral information from these recordings, I am using the following code
> >
> > before_spec<-meanspec(Before_event, f=300000, ovlp=90, plot=FALSE, dB=NULL, norm=FALSE)
> > after_spec <-meanspec(After_event, f=300000, ovlp=90, plot=FALSE, dB=NULL, norm=FALSE)
> >
> > And then I will test for differences between these extracted spectra.
> >
> > Two questions:
> > 1. I have not been able to find the units for the data frame returned by mean spec. Is the unit mV?
> > 2. I would like the returned value to represent absolute energy in each frequency bin over the duration of the recording. I have tried to write the code in a way that achieves this without normalization, but if this is not correct, I would be very grateful to know.
> >
> > Thank you very much for your time, thoughts, and suggestions,
> > Laurel

messages.subject: Re: Calculating entropy index (H)
messages.body_plain:
Ah! Thanks Jerome. I did not know that function existed.

I've been trying to run the entropy function over a matrix composed of 30 s sub-samples of a wav file (using mapply), and I'm having some issues. The function works on the raw data I bring into R via tuneR, but if I try to first calibrate each sub-sample and then create a matrix from the calibrated data, the function fails.

I keep receiving this error message:

Error in seq.default(1, n - wl, wl - (ovlp * wl/100)) :
  wrong sign in 'by' argument

Is it necessary to calibrate before using the entropy functions? I calibrate my data by multiplying each sample by a constant lsb value, which converts the wav data into V.

Thanks,

Sean Hardison

On Monday, July 25, 2016 at 10:38:24 AM UTC-4, Sean Hardison wrote:
> Hi everybody,
>
> I'm trying to determine the entropy index for a sample, and I'm not sure if I'm correctly calculating the PMF for the amplitude envelope. Here's my code:
>
> n = 1.44e6
>
> #amplitude envelope
>
> t_env = env(tr1_upa, f = 48000, envt = "hil", plot = FALSE, norm = FALSE)
>
> #pmf of amplitude envelope
>
> t_env_pmf = abs(t_env)/sum(abs(t_env))
>
> #temporal entropy (Ht)
> Ht = -sum(t_env_pmf * log2(t_env_pmf)*(log2(n))^-1)
>
> #frequency spectrum
>
> m_s = meanspec(tr1_upa, f = 48000, wl = 512, PMF = TRUE, ovlp = 25)
>
> #spectral entropy (Hf)
> Hf = -sum(m_s[,2] * log2(m_s[,2]) * log2(512)^-1)
>
> #acoustic diversity (H)
> H = Hf * Ht
>
> Am I on the right track?
>
> Thanks,
>
> Sean Hardison
